_README: Adjudication of UNTYPED weapon/off-hand proc names for the Utility tier (#91). The candidate rule in src/utility_procs.py is 'untyped + numeric + well-formed + every carrying slot is Weapon/Off Hand' - the deliberate complement of src/untyped_rankable.py's worn-slot rule, so the two gates' populations are disjoint. A candidate in NEITHER list fails the build, so a new untyped weapon proc is a reviewed event rather than a silent zero-count. SINCE #343: 'allow' names enter metadata.utility_untyped_admitted ONLY - the presence-path picker entry that makes them individually rankable. They are NO LONGER unioned into metadata.utility_counting_set, so admitting a name here makes it available to rank, not counted by the Utility tier. Two reasons: a proc is a damage-type decision belonging to the weapon choice rather than a distinct win a player feels, and the 24 admitted procs were 86% of the counting set's measured solve cost - keeping them counted put the tier over its 2.0x perf budget once the worn defensive toggles were added. They NEVER enter metadata.rankable_affixes - a declared-credit control on Holy/Vampirism is the documented defect web/dataset.js warns against.
_discipline: exclude-until-verified. Add to 'allow' ONLY with wiki evidence (wiki_url + evidence + verified date) that the name is a player-felt utility effect worth counting. 'unreviewed' is an honest reason and marks the filed backlog; it is not a judgement that the name is noise. An empty 'allow' list counts zero untyped procs - the Bool presence half of the counting set is unaffected.

allow.name: Wild Frenzy
allow.evidence: Rendered page, 2026-09-22: 'Wild Frenzy Effect: This weapon has a tendency to drive those it strikes insane. On vorpal strikes the target will go wild and attack its own allies for 15 seconds if it fails a DC 25 Will save. Enemies driven wild this way, however, have a chance of coming to their senses if damaged.'
allow.reason: #864 — a vorpal-triggered confusion CC (reviewed 2026-09-22). Quarantined then only to avoid being the ONLY admitted proc; #864 works the whole backlog, so it is admitted with its peers.
allow.upstream_rename: NOT a new effect: the 397c673 refresh RENAMED upstream's `Wind Frenzy` to `Wild Frenzy`, adopting the wiki's own spelling (the page is titled Wild Frenzy and lists I:Insanity as a carrier). Same three carriers as before — Insanity, Madness of the Demon Lords, Legendary Madness of the Demon Lords. `Wind Frenzy` sits in this shard's _retired_2026_08_18 block, retired when upstream typed every instance Bool. It re-enters the untyped-proc population because the refresh ALSO moved the two Madness tiers from `Bool 1` to untyped numerics (50 / 122) while Insanity stayed Bool; the numeric pair is what trips the candidate rule.

quarantined.name: Maximum Charge Tier
quarantined.reason: #864 REVIEWED 2026-10-17 — not an effect. ddowiki Rune Arm: 'The weapon uses Charges with five tiers, and these charges increase in damage the higher the tier (Rune Arms have a max tier level).' It is the rune arm's own blast mechanic, carried by 129 of them; ranking it would rank 'wears a rune arm'. Stays quarantined by ruling.

quarantined.name: Rune Arm Imbue: Bludgeon IV, Fire
quarantined.reason: #864 REVIEWED 2026-10-17 — a real DUAL imbue (Glass Cannon: 'Rune Arm Imbue: Bludgeon V, Fire V: ... 2d8 + 2d10 points of bludgeon/fire damage per hit'), but upstream's name is a mangled compound that is neither type: a player ranking Fire or Bludgeon would not reach it, and admitting it would offer a third, meaningless name. Stays quarantined until the compound is split.

_retired_2026_08_18.why: #374/U4 — the 2026-08-18 refresh re-encoded the type field and gave these procs a real `Bool` type (two exceptions noted per-entry).
